frame: Equatorial J2000, Sol at origin, +X towards RA 0h, +Z towards the north celestial pole
sources: data/galaxies.csv (positions from NED/SIMBAD; distances from the reference given per object, Hubble-flow distances use H0 = 70 km/s/Mpc)
OpenNGC by Mattia Verga, https://github.com/mattiaverga/OpenNGC (CC BY-SA 4.0); adapted subset in data/galaxies-opengnc.csv; https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/
HIZOA-S, Staveley-Smith et al. (2016), AJ 151, 52; https://doi.org/10.26093/cds/vizier.51510052; published tables 2 and 3, bundled VizieR TSV snapshots

galaxies.name: Sagittarius Dwarf Spheroidal
galaxies.distance_ref: McConnachie 2012
galaxies.notes: Closest known satellite galaxy, being torn apart into a stream that wraps around the Milky Way.

galaxies.name: Large Magellanic Cloud
galaxies.distance_ref: Pietrzyński+ 2019 (eclipsing binaries)
galaxies.notes: Largest Milky Way satellite; home of the Tarantula Nebula and SN 1987A.

galaxies.name: Small Magellanic Cloud
galaxies.distance_ref: Graczyk+ 2020 (eclipsing binaries)
galaxies.notes: Gas-rich dwarf irregular, tidally stretched by the LMC and the Milky Way.

galaxies.name: Boötes I
galaxies.distance_ref: McConnachie 2012
galaxies.notes: Ultra-faint dwarf discovered in SDSS data (2006); one of the most dark-matter dominated systems known.

galaxies.name: Draco Dwarf
galaxies.distance_ref: McConnachie 2012
galaxies.notes: Very dark-matter dominated satellite.

galaxies.name: Ursa Minor Dwarf
galaxies.distance_ref: McConnachie 2012
galaxies.notes: One of the oldest stellar populations of any Milky Way satellite.

galaxies.name: Sculptor Dwarf
galaxies.distance_ref: McConnachie 2012
galaxies.notes: First dwarf spheroidal discovered (Shapley 1937).

galaxies.name: Sextans Dwarf
galaxies.distance_ref: McConnachie 2012
galaxies.notes: Very low surface brightness satellite found in 1990.

galaxies.name: Carina Dwarf
galaxies.distance_ref: McConnachie 2012
galaxies.notes: Shows several distinct episodes of star formation.

galaxies.name: Fornax Dwarf
galaxies.distance_ref: McConnachie 2012
galaxies.notes: Brightest Milky Way dwarf spheroidal; has six globular clusters of its own.

galaxies.name: Leo II
galaxies.distance_ref: McConnachie 2012
galaxies.notes: Distant Milky Way satellite.

galaxies.name: Leo I
galaxies.distance_ref: McConnachie 2012
galaxies.notes: Distant, fast-moving satellite seen right next to Regulus on the sky.

galaxies.name: Phoenix Dwarf
galaxies.distance_ref: McConnachie 2012
galaxies.notes: Transition-type dwarf on the edge of the Local Group.

galaxies.name: NGC 6822
galaxies.distance_ref: McConnachie 2012
galaxies.notes: Barred dwarf irregular with bright H II regions.

galaxies.name: NGC 185
galaxies.distance_ref: McConnachie 2012
galaxies.notes: Dwarf elliptical satellite of Andromeda.

galaxies.name: NGC 147
galaxies.distance_ref: McConnachie 2012
galaxies.notes: Dwarf elliptical satellite of Andromeda.

galaxies.name: IC 1613
galaxies.distance_ref: McConnachie 2012
galaxies.notes: Isolated dwarf irregular with very little dust.

galaxies.name: Andromeda Galaxy
galaxies.distance_ref: Li+ 2021 (Cepheids)
galaxies.notes: Nearest large galaxy and the most massive member of the Local Group; will merge with the Milky Way in ~4.5 billion years.

galaxies.name: M32
galaxies.distance_ref: McConnachie 2012
galaxies.notes: Compact elliptical satellite of Andromeda.

galaxies.name: IC 10
galaxies.distance_ref: McConnachie 2012
galaxies.notes: The only starburst galaxy in the Local Group.

galaxies.name: Leo A
galaxies.distance_ref: McConnachie 2012
galaxies.notes: Isolated dwarf dominated by young stars.

galaxies.name: M110
galaxies.distance_ref: McConnachie 2012
galaxies.notes: Bright dwarf elliptical satellite of Andromeda.

galaxies.name: Triangulum Galaxy
galaxies.distance_ref: Breuval+ 2023 (Cepheids)
galaxies.notes: Third-largest Local Group galaxy; hosts the giant H II region NGC 604.

galaxies.name: Wolf-Lundmark-Melotte
galaxies.distance_ref: McConnachie 2012
galaxies.notes: Isolated dwarf irregular on the outskirts of the Local Group.

galaxies.name: Sextans A
galaxies.distance_ref: Tully+ 2013 (Cosmicflows-2)
galaxies.notes: Square-looking dwarf just beyond the Local Group.
